title: Replicating ELEPHANT Social Sycophancy on Instruction-Tuned vs. Base Models
original_idea: Run ELEPHANT scenarios on base (non-instruction-tuned) and instruction-tuned variants of the same models. Compare social sycophancy rates to isolate the contribution of instruction tuning.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Isolating whether sycophancy comes from pre-training vs instruction tuning directly informs mitigation strategy. High diagnostic value.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Running base models requires understanding of completion-style prompting (different from chat). ELEPHANT benchmark setup adds moderate complexity.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Could focus on one model family (e.g., Llama base vs instruct) with a subset of ELEPHANT. Feasible if well-scoped but requires careful setup.

novelty.reasoning: ELEPHANT (arxiv 2505.13995) tested instruction-tuned models and applied ITI (Inference-Time Intervention) on Llama-8B and Llama-70B models tuned for truthfulness. The paper found the 8B model remains highly sycophantic while the 70B model is much less so. DPO-based mitigations (DPO-Validation, DPO-Indirectness) were tested with mixed results. However, a direct comparison of base (non-instruction-tuned) vs. instruction-tuned variants of the same model on ELEPHANT specifically to isolate instruction tuning's contribution has not been the primary focus of published work. The ELEPHANT authors focused on instruction-tuned models. Running base Llama completions on ELEPHANT scenarios would add diagnostic value, though it requires different prompting strategies.
